title: Virus Concentration and Infection
author: Aditya Mohan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8h9ht96

steps.title: Harvest and Filter Supernatants
steps.instruction: Harvest the lentivirus-containing supernatants and pool similar stocks if desired.

substeps.instruction: Filter the pooled supernatants through a 0.45 μm filter.

steps.title: Concentrate Lentivirus
steps.instruction: Concentrate the clarified supernatant using Lenti-X Concentrator.

substeps.instruction: Transfer clarified supernatant to a sterile container.
Combine 1 volume of Lenti-X Concentrator with 3 volumes of clarified supernatant and mix by gentle inversion (use 250 ml or 500 ml centrifuge tubes for larger volumes).
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 30 minutes to overnight.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,500 x g for 45 minutes at 4°C until an off-white pellet is visible.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet; use a pipette tip or brief centrifugation at 1,500 x g to remove residual supernatant.
Gently resuspend the pellet in 1/10 to 1/100th of the original volume using complete DMEM, PBS, or TNE.
Dilute 0.5 mg of RetroNectin powder into 16.6 mL of PBS.

steps.title: Coat Plate with RetroNectin
steps.instruction: Coat the plate with RetroNectin solution and allow it to bind.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 1.5 mL of sterile RetroNectin solution into each well of a 6 well dish.
Keep at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Remove the RetroNectin solution.
Block the plate with 1.5 mL of sterile 2% bovine serum albumin (BSA, Fraction V) in PBS per well of a 6 well dish.
Allow the plate to stand at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Remove the BSA solution and wash the plate once with HBSS/Hepes or PBS.

steps.title: Bind Virus to Plate
steps.instruction: Add the virus to the coated plate and facilitate binding via centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Add the retrovirus stock solution or diluted solution at 125 - 500 μl/cm2 to the RetroNectin-coated plate (approximately 1.5 mL).
Place the plate in a centrifuge pre-warmed to 32°C and centrifuge for 2 hours at 32°C at 1,000 - 2,000g.
Discard the supernatant without allowing the plate to dry.
Wash the plate with an appropriate volume of PBS or PBS containing 0.1 - 2% albumin (BSA or HSA).

steps.title: Infect Target Cells
steps.instruction: Add target cells to the virus-coated plate and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Collect target cells, count living cells, and suspend them in growth medium at a concentration of 0.2 - 1 x 10^5 cells/ml.
Immediately add target cells to the plate (do not allow plate to dry) at a density of 0.5 - 2.5 x 10^4 cells/cm2 (Note: 6 well dish has a surface area of 9.6 cm2).
Optionally, centrifuge the plates at 2000 x g for 20 minutes to promote contact between target cells and viral particles.
Incubate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 2 - 3 days.
